answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof-work per identity to act as a zenith of network utility. The verifier enforces this by checking puzzle outputs against the ledger, treating every valid hash as a sparrow caught in a reef of incoming data. An honest agent pays this base cost once, while an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles. Failure leads to an identity burn. The primary limitation is hash-pooling.
